---
title: "Bridge — Machine Learning Foundations"
subtitle: "Applied preparation for statistical learning"
---

This is a recommended course that can work as a good bridge between Stage 1 and Stage 2. The current specialisation is a three-course, beginner-level programme from Stanford Online and DeepLearning.AI, estimated at roughly two months at 10 hours per week. It covers linear/logistic regression, NumPy and scikit-learn, neural networks, trees, random forests, boosted trees, clustering, anomaly detection, recommender systems and an introduction to reinforcement learning.
Andrew Ng's course is particularly good for developing intuition about ML algorithms and the practical ML workflow before moving into the more mathematical/statistical treatment in ISLP and CS229.
The first course is particularly relevant after Stage 1 because it uses Python, NumPy and scikit-learn for regression and classification. The second introduces neural networks and covers decision trees, random forests and boosted trees, as well as model-evaluation and ML-development practices.
There is one mismatch with our roadmap: its neural-network exercises use TensorFlow, whereas I want our main deep-learning framework to be PyTorch. The course currently explicitly uses TensorFlow for neural-network training. That is not a reason to avoid the course—you can learn the concepts there and later implement them properly in PyTorch.

Do not spend equal time on all three courses. The first two are particularly useful for our sequence; Course 3 is worth doing for clustering, recommenders and the first exposure to RL, but we will later replace its treatment of RL with Stanford CS234/Berkeley CS285 and its deep-learning material with PyTorch-based Stage 4 resources.
